 Our Mission 

 Coventry University is a global Education Group that empowers students and communities to transform their lives and society through teaching, learning, research, and enterprise.

 An ambitious and innovative university, our research is designed to have real-world impact on society and tackle global challenges through our 13 challenge-led, interdisciplinary research centres. We enable high performing research teams and future research leaders to thrive and make an impact locally, regionally, nationally, and globally. 

 The Role 

 Coventry University is seeking a motivated and talented Research Fellow to join an industry-led collaborative research project focused on battery intelligence for battery energy storage systems (BESSs). The project will investigate advanced battery testing, modelling, and intelligent state estimation, with an emphasis on physics-guided artificial intelligence (AI).

 Fully funded by Innovate UK for 12 months starting February 1st 2027, the project brings together academic expertise and industrial requirements to develop and validate innovative approaches to battery performance assessment, condition monitoring, and state estimation. Based at Coventry University working closely with two industry partners to address practical challenges in battery characterisation, operational monitoring, and intelligent battery management system (BMS).

 Focusing on battery testing and data analysis, battery modelling, and the development and validation of AI-enabled algorithms for estimating battery state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH). You will contribute to experimental investigations, model development, algorithm implementation, and the validation of research outcomes using laboratory measurements and, where available, real-world operational data. 

 Qualifications 

 PhD in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, Energy Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline; or a relevant bachelor's or master's degree combined with equivalent relevant research or industrial experience.

 Our Successful Candidate 

 You will need expertise in lithium-ion batteries, BMS, battery performance and ageing. You will have a strong research track record, including high-quality publications, successful collaboration across multidisciplinary teams, and experience developing research proposals and projects. Advanced knowledge of research methods and regulatory compliance is essential.

 Candidates with expertise in combining physics-based battery modelling and AI-driven approaches to develop robust battery state-estimation methods are particularly encouraged to apply. Knowledge of LFP batteries, including voltage hysteresis and flat open-circuit voltage characteristics, would be advantageous.

 The Benefits 

 As a staff member of Coventry University, you will have access to a wide range of industry leading rewards and benefits which includes:

 Excellent Employers Pension Contribution

 30 days Annual leave plus Bank Holidays

 New Holiday Purchase Scheme up to 5 additional days

 Life Assurance 4x Salary

 BUPA Cash Plan

 50% off Tuition Fees for staff dependants

 CU Reward Scheme – Discounts across a range of High Street/ Online Retailers

 Cycle To Work scheme

 Our Culture 

 As a global Education Group, equality, diversity, and inclusion are embedded within the fabric of our organisation and are a key focus of our core values. We harness the power and potential of the diverse cultures, backgrounds, abilities, and experiences of our students, colleagues, and partners to create opportunities for all.

 The Bristol Business School of the University of the West of England (UWE Bristol) invites applications for a Doctoral Researcher position in the MSCA Doctoral Network MINARET: A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Cultures. 

 Project Overview 

 This doctoral position is part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Cultures (MINARET), funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe programme.

 MINARET brings together leading universities and research partner institutions to train 15 doctoral candidates investigating the relationships between law, religion, economy and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies. The network's three core aims are to advance empirical and theoretical understanding of the interactions between law, religion, economy and governance; to deliver sustainable, interdisciplinary doctoral training across disciplines, sectors, and regions; and to contribute to global debates on democratisation and good governance through policy-relevant research, publications, workshops, and outreach activities.

 PhD Topic Description 

 The doctoral project (DC9) at UWE Bristol forms part of MINARET's work package on law, economy, and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies. It will examine how Islamic finance institutions contribute to public trust, economic governance, and constitutional legitimacy in Central Asia and Southeast Asia (Uzbekistan and Indonesia).

 The research focuses on how Islamic principles such as fairness, risk-sharing, and social responsibility are translated into contemporary legal, financial, and governance arrangements. It will explore how Islamic finance institutions interact with state structures, influence governance practices, and shape citizens' perceptions of state authority and institutional legitimacy. The project aims to bridge debates in economics, law, governance, political economy, and Islamic studies by generating new empirical and theoretical insights into the relationship between religion, economy, and governance.

 Host Institution 

 The Bristol Business School is renowned for research across economics, governance, public policy, and international development, offering a vibrant and inclusive research culture. Research group Bristol Research in Economics (BRE) is an internationally recognised cluster of leading economists pursuing innovative research in intersecting areas of economics including applied economics, development economics, political economy and regional studies.

 Essential Skills & Qualifications 

 A relevant master’s degree relating to economics, economic development, development studies, behavioural science, or a related field.

 Excellent English speaking, reading, and writing skills (applicants will need IELTS score of 7.0 overall, or equivalent).

 Strong mixed-methods research skills.

 Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.

 Effective communication skills for academic and non-academic audiences.

 Motivation to engage in interdisciplinary research and policy outreach.

 Desirable 

 Experience integrating methods and theories from multiple disciplines.

 Experience working with both quantitative and qualitative data.

 Salary & Eligibility 

 You will be employed on a 36-month contract under the conditions of the MSCA Doctoral Network scheme which includes: gross salary of €4,008/month (approx. £3,447/month); mobility allowance of €489/month (approx. £421/month); and family allowance of €455/month (approx. £391/month), if applicable. 

 Eligibility conditions 

 You must not already hold a doctoral degree.

 You must have an IELTS score of 7.0 overall or equivalent.

 You must not have lived or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the UK for more than 12 months in the 36 months before your recruitment date.

 You can be of any nationality.

 Where is this role based? 

 This post is based at our lively Frenchay campus.

Research Fellow in Sustainable Process Engineering

Do you have a strong interest in sustainable processes? Do you have experience in Process Systems Engineering and Sustainability? Are you keen to develop your career in optimising novel separations? Do you want to join one of the UK’s research Intensive Universities?

A key challenge in decarbonising pharmaceutical manufacturing is the production of high-purity solvents required for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) synthesis, chromatography and cleaning operations. Existing bio-based solvents often fail to meet the stringent moisture, purity and quality specifications demanded by the pharmaceutical sector, while conventional purification methods are highly energy intensive and economically prohibitive.

In this project, you will focus on the development, optimisation and scale-up of advanced solvent production and purification processes, integrating novel membrane separation technologies, process design and mathematical models to deliver pharmaceutical-grade solvents at industrially relevant scales. The work will involve process design, separation and dehydration system optimisation, mass and energy integration, and integrated process performance and evaluation. These activities will establish scalable manufacturing routes that reduce energy consumption, improve resource efficiency and enable the production of low-carbon solvents suitable for deployment across global medicines manufacturing supply chains.

This project is funded via the InnovateUK Industrialising UK Bio-based Solvents for Global Medicine Manufacturing, with partners across the University of Leeds, Queen Mary University London, Exactmer Limited, Celtic Renewables Limited, OXCCU Tech LTD, Solve Chemistry LTD, Atmospheric AI Limited and the Centre for Process Innovation Limited.

What we offer in return

26 days holiday plus approx.16 Bank Holidays/days that the University is closed by custom (including Christmas) – That’s 42 days a year!
Generous pension scheme plus life assurance– the University contributes 14.5% of salary
Health and Wellbeing: Discounted staff membership options at The Edge, our state-of-the-art Campus gym, with a pool, sauna, climbing wall, cycle circuit, and sports halls.
Personal Development: Access to courses run by our Organisational Development & Professional Learning team.
Access to on-site childcare, shopping discounts and travel schemes are also available.

And much more! 

To explore the post further or for any queries you may have, please contact: 

Dr. Keeran Ward, Associate Professor in Chemical Engineering

 We are seeking two ambitious postdoctoral machine-learning researchers to join the Spatial and Translational Pathology Group at the University of Oxford. These 24-month posts will develop advanced AI models using a unique, large-scale collection of multimodal NHS clinical data, including electronic health records, laboratory and molecular data, medical imaging and digital pathology.

 The posts form part of a multidisciplinary programme in computational pathology and clinical AI supported by the MPN Research Foundation, Blood Cancer UK, Cancer Research UK and Wellcome. The successful candidates will develop and validate advanced machine-learning approaches using large-scale multimodal clinical, molecular and imaging data, with applications including personalised prediction of disease progression, treatment response and patient outcomes.

 One of the posts will have a particular focus on a major MPN Research Foundation programme establishing a multimodal NHS data resource for approximately 5,000 patients with, or investigated for, myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs).

 We are particularly interested in candidates with a strong machine-learning, computer-science or engineering background. Prior experience in haematology or pathology is not essential: the successful candidate will work closely with clinician scientists, pathologists, biomedical engineers and computational researchers and will be supported to develop the necessary clinical and biological understanding.

 The role  

 Lead the design, development and validation of machine-learning models integrating multimodal clinical, laboratory, molecular/genomic, imaging and pathology-derived data.

 Develop robust and reproducible pipelines for large-scale, heterogeneous and longitudinal NHS data, including data representation, harmonisation, quality control and linkage within approved secure environments.

 Work closely with the Thames Valley and Surrey Secure Data Environment (TVS SDE) team, with shared learning, knowledge exchange and training to develop secure, reproducible approaches for machine-learning research using large-scale NHS clinical data.

 Develop and evaluate appropriate multimodal learning approaches, including methods for incomplete and temporally structured data, with rigorous comparison against relevant clinical and statistical baselines.

 Work with multidisciplinary collaborators to translate clinical questions into tractable computational problems and interpret model outputs in their biological and clinical context.

 Contribute machine-learning expertise to other closely aligned projects within the research group, including reusable code and pipelines, technical advice, and support for research students and colleagues using AI/ML methods.

 Contribute to high-quality publications and present findings at national and international scientific meetings.

 About you 

 You will hold, or be close to completion of, a PhD/DPhil in machine learning, computer science, engineering or a related quantitative discipline. You should have:

 Strong programming skills in Python.

 Experience developing and evaluating machine-learning or deep-learning models.

 Experience working with large, complex and/or multimodal datasets.

 Ability to work effectively and communicate within a multidisciplinary research team.

 Experience with clinical or healthcare data, multimodal machine learning, biomedical AI, digital pathology or secure data environments would be advantageous but is not essential.

 Research environment 

 The postholder will join the Spatial and Translational Pathology Group within the Nuffield Division of Clinical Laboratory Sciences, Radcliffe Department of Medicine. The programme brings together expertise in clinical haematology, pathology, biomedical engineering, machine learning and data science, with access to large-scale NHS data and University high-performance CPU/GPU computing infrastructure. The postholder will work in close partnership with the Thames Valley and Surrey SDE team and will benefit from shared learning and training in secure, large-scale NHS data research.

 The University of Oxford is committed to equality of opportunity and welcomes applications from all backgrounds.

Research Fellow – Bioinformatics and Data Sciences

The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. 

We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee.  

Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference.   

The role

This is an exciting new opportunity for an enthusiastic and motivated postdoctoral fellow in health data-sciences and biomedical informatics to join the Veterinary Health Innovation Engine (vHive) and the University of Surrey’s Health and Biomedical Informatics Group. 

The overall objective for the postholder is to work within these multidisciplinary teams to apply and repurpose techniques in informatics, data sciences, machine learning and AI, to develop new insights and approaches to improve animal health and welfare. This will include assuming responsibilities for informatics- and computational-led data analysis to identify new opportunities via market analysis, drug repurposing/discovery, formal knowledge representation, and precision medicine-led biomarker discovery to complement new therapeutic veterinary medicine approaches.  

This work is contextualised into a programme award from our sponsors Zoetis (the largest animal health corporation globally) that seeks to support their interests in key disease issues. The post will thus involve collaborative working with industry partners, charities, as well as other universities and research institutes across the UK and internationally. The job holder will develop, repurpose and use new research techniques and methods, in consultation with the research supervisor and with input from Zoetis employees. These studies will include assessing interview and stakeholder data for unmet need definition, in-silico drug repurposing and trial research, critical evaluation and interpretation of biomarker discovery datasets (and in particular proteomics and transcriptomics), plus extensive library research. 

The overall programme of research will be jointly developed by Prof. Nophar Geifman and the person appointed. There are opportunities to broaden out into other areas such as new algorithm development, and advanced computational methodologies for integrated analyses. 

About you

You will have a key role in planning, designing and executing a range of analyses on varied novel projects aimed at high-impact and theoretically valuable research questions. Strong quantitative research skills with hands-on real-world experience are essential. You must have experience in the application of informatics pipelines to health and biomedical data (outside educational settings). You will need good communication skills, and able to work with and disseminate information to both academic and non-academic audiences. You will have a PhD in health, medical or bio-informatics, epidemiology, data sciences, or a related subject, ideally with a focus on utilising large-scale health/biomedical data and the application of advanced data analysis methods such as machine-learning. Equivalent research or industry experience will also be considered. Excellent statistical and analytical skills are necessary, as are programming skills, ideally with the ability to work in R and experience with bioinformatic tools/software. Coding in other languages such as python, is an advantage.

How to apply

Please complete the online application form, and attach a complete CV inclusive of publication list, as well as a cover letter. We value authentic, human-written insights, so please refrain from using generative AI tools when applying.

WMS offers academic education across several levels and is the UK leader for graduate entry medicine.  Our portfolio of postgraduate programmes aims to provide excellent education and continued professional development for healthcare professionals across a number of areas, including advanced clinical and critical care practice, diabetes, leadership, medical education, interdisciplinary biomedical research, public health and health research.  We have expanded our education portfolio to include two innovative undergraduate courses: MSci Integrated Natural Sciences and BSc Health and Medical Sciences.  We also offer full and part time research degrees either at Warwick Medical School or in a clinical setting, encompassing PhDs, MD Doctor of Medicine, PhD by Published Work, and MSc by Research.

 Type of Contract : Project-limited for three years from 4 August 2027

 We seek to appoint an enthusiastic, motivated clinical research fellow with strong interest in pursuing an academic path in cardiovascular medicine. The successful candidate will join the dynamic Cardiology research group within the Faculty of Medicine, headed by Professor Dana Dawson.

 This is a 3-year post (start date August 2027), funded through a British Heart Foundation Program Grant to explore the unique mechanistic patho-physiology of the strongest psycho-somatic interaction known in medicine. Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (or ‘broken heart syndrome’) is an acute cardiac emergency which predominantly affects women (90%) and is triggered by a precipitant episode of stress. Despite non-obstructed coronary arteries there is severe heart dysfunction, and although the pump function ‘normalises’ shortly afterwards, these patients have reduced long-term survival. This programme of research will combine state-of-the-art translational and clinical research methodology to investigate candidate pathophysiological mechanisms in takotsubo cardiomyopathy.

 The appointee will be part of a translational team and work closely with immunology, thrombosis/fibrinolysis, bioinformatics and clinical colleagues. It is hoped that together, the group will provide the leap of science required to understand the full pathway in which this newly described disease triggers and unfolds.

 The Clinical Research Fellow will be responsible for early identification of patients with acute takotsubo cardiomyopathy and acute myocardial infarction, and for this purpose foster close links with the acute cardiology wards and the cardiac catheterisation laboratory. The appointee will ensure early consent (or ascent) of potential study participants and be responsible for coordination, organisation and completion of both invasive and non-invasive study investigations. They will plan and execute all clinical research investigations, such as collection of blood and preparation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, set-up of invasive coronary physiology and endomyocardial biopsy studies with the relevant specialist consultants, set-up of advanced cardiac magnetic resonance, field cycling magnetic resonance imaging, and specific molecular tracer-enabled positron emission tomography with specialist consultants and medical physicists in Aberdeen and Edinburgh . The appointee will be encouraged to learn translational experimentation and work in collaboration with post-doctoral immunology and thrombosis scientist fellows, to develop their laboratory skills if they demonstrate talent and aptitude in this direction. Training will be provided for all aspects of the work. You will be encouraged to attend relevant training courses.

 Salary will be at the appropriate point on the Clinical scale for Academics below level of Consultant, £52,229 - £68,184 per annum, and negotiable with placement according to qualifications and experience.

 Information on other visa options is available at https://www.gov.uk/check-uk-visa .

 Please do not hesitate to contact Grant Rae, HR Adviser (e-mail: grant.rae@abdn.ac.uk ) for further information.

The Department of Paediatrics is a world leader in child health research and hosts internationally renowned research programmes in drug development, gastroenterology, haematology, HIV, immunology, neuroimaging, neuromuscular diseases, paediatric oncology and vaccinology.

Our work combines large-scale computational analyses and computational methods development, with the design of novel experimental technologies.  We work closely with other labs and clinicians across the UK and overseas, and co-lead national initiatives focused on paediatric oncology, such as the Stratified Medicine Paediatrics (SMPaeds) programme. Recent work from the group includes the discovery of Loss Translocation amplification chromothripsis, the rearrangement mechanism driving the onset and evolution of high-grade osteosarcoma, and the development of SIMMA, a single-molecule liquid biopsy assay based on nanopore sequencing. The Cortes-Ciriano group offers extensive opportunities for collaboration and specialised training in computational cancer genomics. You will benefit from scientific guidance and mentorship designed to foster your development towards achieving scientific independence. This commitment is reflected in the success of former Postdoctoral Fellows from the group, several of whom now lead their own research groups at leading industry and academic organizations. 

 This position is offered full-time on a fixed-term contract initially for two years with the possibility to extend provided further external funding is available. 

 This role may be eligible for Global Talent Visa.

 About you  

 You will have a PhD in a quantitative discipline, such as, but not limited to, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics or Computer Science, supplemented by relevant post-qualification experience in a research role. You will have a strong, demonstrable track record in data science and programming, evidenced by your publication record and contributions to research projects. You will possess experience in computational data analysis. Experience in genomics and cancer biology are desirable but not essential.  You will have highly effective verbal and written communication skills with all level of staff staff and an ability to operate effectively in a demanding, multidisciplinary and collaborative research environment. Strong intrinsic motivation and an unwavering passion for advancing paediatric cancer research, driving innovation, and collaborating with interdisciplinary teams in an international research environment are essential.

Role:  Research Associate in Coastal Dynamic Management

Job Purpose:

The postholder will support the project “Coastal-Twin AI for Dynamic shorelinEs Management” (C-TIDE), funded by the Natural Environment Research Council (NERC), UKRI to develop an AI-enabled digital twin for coastal shoreline management in Northern Ireland.

The Research Associate will be working on the technical pipeline: acquiring and harmonising the project’s coastal datasets, contributing to the development and validation of the proposed AI models for shoreline detection and morphodynamics, integrating these into the decision-support digital twin, and supporting the human-in-the-loop and reporting workstreams.

C-TIDE is addressing the lack of a strategic Shoreline Management Plan for Northern Ireland’s coastline, which faces increasing storm frequency, wave action and sea-level rise. Led by Ulster University, the project is building a unified AI-ready coastal data platform, label-efficient machine learning models for shoreline and morphodynamic prediction, and a geospatial digital twin with human-in-the-loop decision support – transforming how the region observes, forecasts and manages its dynamic coastline. C-TIDE vision is to create the first dynamic, AI enabled coastal Digital Twins for NI, delivering real-time shoreline intelligence and transparent, auditable decision-support for adaptive coastal management. C-TIDE will further establish a multidisciplinary community of oceanographers, climate scientists, engineers, AI specialists, policymakers, and local authorities, ensuring that the platform is user-informed, scientifically robust, and scalable across the UK and internationally.

 We are recruiting a postdoctoral researcher to support work on an ESRC supported project entitled 'Spontaneous movement to music in toddlers'.

 Learning to align movement with sound is a crucial skill for social cognition, supporting conversational turn-taking and musical performance. Parents report that 90% of children dance to music by 12 months. The early emergence of dance to music, its cross-cultural ubiquity, and its absence in non-human primates suggests that it is a core element of what it means to be human. However, spontaneous dancing to music in toddlers has not previously been studied in the laboratory. As a result, we know little about the form and function of dance in toddlers. In this project, we will use optical motion tracking and EEG to investigate why and how toddlers dance to music.

 We are looking for a researcher to work under the supervision of Prof Adam Tierney, Prof Denis Mareschal, and Prof Elisa Ferrè. The project will use a variety of methods, including EEG, optical motion tracking, and behavioural testing. The ideal candidate will have experience in both EEG and motion tracking, as well as experience with testing infants and/or young children.

 You will:

 a) collaborate in the design and piloting of the experimental protocols and analysis techniques

 b) recruit participants

 c) conduct testing

 d) preprocess and analyse data, and

 e) lead the write up of study results.

 This role is offered on a fixed-term basis from 1 February 2027 through 31 January 2029.

 This is a full-time role, working 35 hours per week.

 Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory enhanced check with the Disclosure and Barring Service.

 Interviews will be held on 11 January 2027.

 Grade 7 of the College's London Pay Scale which is £45,132 rising to £51,387 per annum.

 Birkbeck offers a competitive salary and pension scheme, 31 days paid leave, flexible working arrangements and some of the most generous benefits in the HE sector, all while being located right in the heart of Central London.

 The salary quoted is on the College's London Pay Scale which includes a consolidated Weighting/Allowance which applies only to staff whose normal contractual place of work is in the London area.

While we are happy to respond to all informal enquiries, only formal applications through the online system will be considered.

 Edinburgh Napier University’s School of Applied Sciences is committed to providing an environment that recognises and supports research excellence. 

 Currently, our Criminology subject group are working in collaboration with the Chief Scientist Office Scotland on the delivery of the Crime and Criminal Justice as Social Determinants of Health in Scotland project. 

 As such, we now have an opportunity for a Research Assistant to join the project to support a period of maternity cover, and play an important role in the collection/management of data, while assisting with analysis and interpretation of results. 

 The Role:   

 As Research Assistant you will have the opportunity to join a team of experienced researchers, who will be investigating digital healthcare provisions in prisons and undertaking studies to understand the different experiences of service users within those facilities. 

 You will be in an ideal position to use your skills and experience of gathering data for research to help set up and administer these studies, collect and manage data, and assist with interpreting results. 

 This process will involve interviews with senior policy makers, as well as focus groups with individuals currently serving residency, to talk about their experiences in healthcare and provide valuable insight into their effectiveness. 

 The role will also give you the chance to use your strong written and verbal communication skills to contribute to the production of research reports and publications and present information on research progress/outcomes to various stakeholders. 

 With this in mind, this post will be an excellent opportunity for you take the first step towards your research or career in Criminology, as it will equip you with useful knowledge and skills in research methods and techniques that will serve you well in the future.

 Master's degree in a relevant social science discipline

 Undergraduate degree in Criminology, Sociology, Social Policy, Public Health or a related social science discipline

 Recent experience of conducting health-related research

 Training or academic experience in qualitative research methods and data analysis

 Experience of participant recruitment

 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentation and report writing skills

 The project is led by Dr Jiabao Xu with Professor Huabing Yin. PEEN places the resolving power in the sample chemistry rather than the optics: bacterial cells are physically expanded in a hydrogel that retains their biomolecules, and silver nanoparticles are then grown inside the expanded gel to create a three-dimensional surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate.

 In addition, the postholder will also be expected to contribute to the formulation and submission of research publications and research proposals as well as help manage and direct this complex and challenging project as opportunities allow.

Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Imaging: from radio astronomy to magnetic resonance imaging in medicine
Edinburgh, Midlothian, United Kingdom

Role: 
Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Imaging: from radio astronomy to magnetic resonance imaging in medicine 

Contract: 
Full-time (35 hours per week), Fixed Term
 
Contract for 18 Months
 

Salary: 
Grade 7 - £38,448 - £48,337 per annum

Holiday Entitlement: 
33 days annual leave, plus 9 buildings closed days for all full-time staff.

Detailed Description 

The Biomedical and Astronomical Signal Processing (
BASP
) Laboratory at 
Heriot-Watt University
, Edinburgh, is recruiting a multidisciplinary team of postdoctoral researchers to develop next-generation computational imaging algorithms, from fundamental theory and methods to transformative applications in radio astronomy and medical imaging. The start date is March 05, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

BASP’s research spans the full spectrum of computational imaging, from mathematical foundations and algorithm development to high-impact scientific and medical applications.

Multiple positions are available through research projects awarded to Professor 
Yves Wiaux
, Head of BASP, by the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC), through the AI-CLEAN project, and the Oxford Breakthrough Listen Hub, through the XIRI project. These projects aim to advance the next generation of computational imaging algorithms for radio astronomy, with the potential for technology transfer to medical imaging.

The overarching ambition is to harness cutting-edge AI to deliver a new generation of computational imaging algorithms combining unprecedented precision, robustness, computational efficiency and scalability. The primary application is extreme-scale radio-interferometric imaging for next-generation facilities such as the 
Square Kilometre Array (SKA)
, with subsequent transfer of the developed methodologies to fast, dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Deep learning will provide powerful data-driven representations and reconstruction capabilities, while Agentic AI will enable specialised AI agents to collaborate, assess intermediate results and adapt reconstruction strategies to the data, measurement physics and imaging task. By combining these complementary capabilities, the research will move beyond fixed reconstruction pipelines towards more adaptive, intelligent and reliable imaging algorithms.

A central challenge is to harness the expressive power of deep learning and the adaptability of Agentic AI while preserving the mathematical guarantees, physical interpretability and reliability essential for scientific imaging. The research will develop principled approaches to image estimation and uncertainty quantification, aiming to deliver high-fidelity reconstructions that are not only computationally efficient but also scientifically trustworthy.

Key Duties and Responsibilities 

The postholders will conduct cutting-edge research in computational imaging, contributing to one or more aspects of the projects, from high-dimensional data modelling and imaging algorithm development to high-performance software implementation, validation through simulation, and application to impactful astronomical and medical case studies.

Appointments will typically be for an initial period of 1 year, with the possibility of renewal for up to three years, subject to research progress.

Education, Qualifications and Experience 

‍We are seeking outstanding candidates with a PhD, or close to completion, in astronomy, physics, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, computer science or a related discipline.

Candidates should have expertise in computational imaging and/or in one of the target application domains: radio interferometry or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

Essential Criteria

A PhD, or near completion of a PhD, in a relevant discipline.

Expertise in computational imaging, radio interferometry or MRI.

Ability to conduct self-directed research and develop innovative solutions.

A strong publication record commensurate with career stage.

Excellent written and oral communication skills.

Desirable Criteria

Experience working in multicultural and multidisciplinary research environments.

Ability to collaborate effectively within a research team.

Demonstrated capacity for independent research and initiative.

Experience in PhD student supervision or mentoring.

How to Apply 

Applications should comprise a single PDF document containing a motivation letter, CV, publication list, and the names and contact details of three referees. 

The PDF should be submitted through the Heriot-Watt University Job Portal.

Applications should be submitted prior to 
Friday 05 March, 2027
. The screening of candidates will start in December 2026 and continue until the positions are filled.

Informal enquiries about the positions are welcome and should be directed to Professor Yves Wiaux at y.wiaux@hw.ac.uk.

Heriot-Watt
 
University is committed to securing equality of opportunity in employment and to the creation of an environment in which individuals are selected, trained, promoted, appraised, and otherwise treated on the sole basis of their relevant merits and abilities.
 
Equality and diversity are all about maximising potential and creating a culture of inclusion for all. 

Heriot-Watt
 
University values diversity across our university community and welcomes applications from all sectors of society, particularly from underrepresented groups. For more information, please see our website
 
https://www.hw.ac.uk/uk/services/equality-diversity.htm
 
and also our award-winning work in Disability Inclusive Science Careers
 
https://disc.hw.ac.uk/
 
. 

Use our total rewards calculator:
 
https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm
 
to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University.

About Heriot-Watt University 

At Heriot-Watt we are passionate about our values and look to them to connect our people globally and to help us collaborate and celebrate our success through working together. Our research programmes can deliver real world impact which is achieved through the diversity of our international community and the recognition of creative talent that connects our global team.

Our flourishing community will give you the freedom to challenge and to bring your enterprising mind and to help our partners with solutions that can be applied now and in the future. Join us and Heriot Watt will provide you with a platform to thrive and work in a way that also helps you live your life in balance with well-being and inclusiveness at the heart of our global community.

 About the Role 

 We are seeking an enthusiastic Research Assistant, to join the newly established Nicholson Lab . The postholder will support a project investigating how glioblastoma cells change state and acquire resistance to treatment. They will perform cancer cell culture, CRISPR–Cas9 editing and drug-response experiments, and help generate single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets following genetic and pharmacological perturbation. Working closely with Dr James Nicholson, they will contribute to experimental planning, data collection and interpretation, and the effective day-to-day delivery of the project. This well-resourced project combines computational discovery with experimental validation to identify regulators of glioblastoma cell plasticity and treatment resistance, with the longer-term aim of developing strategies to prevent tumour recurrence.

 About You 

 You will hold a degree in biological sciences, cancer biology, molecular biology or a related subject. Experience in mammalian cell culture and common molecular biology techniques would be advantageous, although extensive prior research experience is not required. You should be enthusiastic about experimental research, able to work carefully and maintain accurate records, and willing to learn new techniques. Training and support will be provided in the project’s specialist cell-culture, gene-editing and single-cell sequencing methods.

 About the School/Department/Institute/Project 

 The Blizard Institute was established in 2003 and is one of six Institutes within the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry, QMUL. The Institute is comprised of staff based in four academic Centres and one Public Engagement Centre and supports a combined total of c700 postgraduate research and taught students. The Blizard constitutes a world class biomedical research institute that integrates all stages of research from basic science through to clinical studies across a diverse range of fields including genomics, cell biology, translational immunology, neuroscience and trauma. Our research addresses the health needs of our local population, while delivering new treatments on a global scale and aims to deliver excellence in all aspects of research, teaching and clinical service. 

 About Queen Mary 

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

 Benefits 

We offer competitive salaries, access to a generous pension scheme, 30 days’ leave per annum (pro-rata for part-time/fixed-term), a season ticket loan scheme and access to a comprehensive range of personal and professional development opportunities. In addition, we offer a range of work life balance and family friendly, inclusive employment policies, flexible working arrangements, and campus facilities.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. Reasonable adjustments will be made at each stage of the recruitment process for any candidate with a disability. We are open to considering applications from candidates wishing to work flexibly.

 We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Research Fellow to join the Salah Elias laboratory at the University of Southampton and lead the experimental research within a BBSRC-funded project investigating mechanisms of mammary epithelial morphogenesis through AI-integrated human organoid models and predictive cell fate mapping. This is an excellent opportunity to shape an innovative project and develop a distinctive interdisciplinary profile at the interface of cell and developmental biology, human organoid models, advanced imaging, molecular phenotyping and computational biology.

 About the project 

 The project combines patient-derived mammary organoids, high-resolution 3D/4D imaging, single-cell transcriptomics and AI-driven analysis and modelling to uncover mechanisms governing epithelial morphogenesis. At its core is a fundamental question: how do polarised cell divisions coordinate luminogenesis with cell fate and differentiation to build and maintain functional epithelial architecture? By addressing this question in physiologically relevant human models, the project aims to define how these mechanisms safeguard epithelial integrity and how their disruption leads to abnormal tissue organisation.

 You will take a central role in the scientific development of this ambitious programme, including experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. You will use patient-derived human mammary organoids and gene loss-of-function approaches, together with high-resolution 3D/4D fluorescence imaging, fate mapping, advanced quantitative analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing, to connect molecular and cellular mechanisms with cell fate and tissue architecture.

 A major strength of the project is the integration of experimental and computational biology. Working with computational researchers, you will integrate multimodal imaging and transcriptomic data into AI-driven mechanistic and predictive models to determine how changes at the level of individual cells influence tissue-level organisation and function.

 About you 

 You will have a PhD, or be close to completing one, in cell biology, developmental biology, stem cell biology or a related discipline.

 You will have strong experimental experience across several relevant areas of cell and developmental biology, which may include organoid or mammalian cell culture, epithelial biology, high-resolution fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology. Experience in advanced automated or semi-automated quantitative image analysis would be particularly valuable. An understanding of computational or mathematical modelling would be advantageous, but is not essential.

 You will be a creative and collaborative scientist with a proactive, analytical approach and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research. You should be able to plan and conduct rigorous experiments, interpret data, troubleshoot methods and communicate findings clearly.

 Alongside leading the experimental research, you will contribute scientific ideas and interpretation, support collaborative projects, help develop grant proposals, prepare research for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, train colleagues in new methods and advise on scientific protocols. You will bring excellent interpersonal skills and work constructively with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines.

 What we offer 

 You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment bringing together expertise in mammary biology, organoids, advanced imaging, single-cell biology, AI and computational modelling. You will have access to state-of-the-art microscopy, flow-cytometry and high-performance computing facilities, multidisciplinary training and career-development opportunities.

 The University of Southampton offers a range of benefits, including a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days. We support flexible working and a healthy work–life balance, alongside access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS), subsidised health and fitness facilities and a range of staff discounts.

 The post is offered on a three-year fixed-term basis.

 For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Salah Elias at S.K.Elias@soton.ac.uk .

 Join the ARIA-funded CoreShell Fibre Foundry programme and turn molecular simulations into practical protein-design rules. You will develop high-throughput Python workflows and descriptors capturing assembly geometry, stability and organisation, working across simulation, machine learning and experiment.

 FTE: 1.0 FTE (full time)

 The Department of Pure and Applied Chemistry is seeking an exceptional and highly motivated Research Associate to join the ARIA-funded CoreShell Fibre Foundry programme.

 The programme aims to develop a new approach to manufacturing hollow inorganic fibres using engineered proteins as reusable molecular fabrication units. This role is central to its computational design framework, translating molecular simulation trajectories into physically meaningful descriptors and practical design rules.

 You will develop high-throughput workflows for analysing coarse-grained molecular-dynamics simulations of candidate protein assemblies.  Working within an interdisciplinary team of computational chemists, machine-learning researchers, protein scientists and engineers, you will:

 extract geometric, topological and structural descriptors from protein-assembly trajectories

 develop structure-property relationships linking protein sequence features to assembly behaviour

 generate reliable descriptor datasets for predictive and active learning models

 compare simulated behaviour with microscopy, scattering and other experimental data

 build robust, documented, reusable and version-controlled Python analysis pipelines

 contribute to project meetings, milestone reports, publications, presentations and research-data management.

 You will have a PhD in computational chemistry, molecular simulation, physics, biophysics, materials modelling, computational biology, mathematics or a closely related discipline. We are recruiting a postdoctoral researcher to support work on an ESRC supported project entitled 'Spontaneous movement to music in toddlers'.

Learning to align movement with sound is a crucial skill for social cognition, supporting conversational turn-taking and musical performance. Parents report that 90% of children dance to music by 12 months. The early emergence of dance to music, its cross-cultural ubiquity, and its absence in non-human primates suggests that it is a core element of what it means to be human. However, spontaneous dancing to music in toddlers has not previously been studied in the laboratory. As a result, we know little about the form and function of dance in toddlers. In this project, we will use optical motion tracking and EEG to investigate why and how toddlers dance to music.

The role

A postdoctoral research position in computational and theoretical photochemistry is available in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol, supported by the ERC Consolidator Grant 101229789 In Silico Photochemistry of Atmospheric Molecules in Aqueous Aerosols (ISPAMIA). The project is led by Prof Basile Curchod (University of Bristol, UK).

This project will investigate the photochemistry of atmospheric volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in and at the surface of aqueous aerosols. The project will comprise (1) theoretical developments to describe the complex environment created by an aqueous aerosol, from an electronic structure and nuclear dynamics perspective, and (2) the application of these methods to simulate the unimolecular and bimolecular photochemistry of selected VOCs in and at the surface of an aqueous aerosol. This project builds on recent works by our research group on studying the gas-phase photochemistry of atmospheric and complex molecules.

The present postdoctoral position will focus on the study of the interaction of selected VOCs with different models of the air-water interface of an aqueous droplet, using machine-learned potentials to accelerate the sampling of ground-state distributions representative of the VOC in different environments.

Further details of the In Silico Photochemistry Group can be found at www.in-silico-photochem.com, where a list of the group’s publication can be found as well.

What will you be doing?

The postdoctoral researcher will be based in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol where they will undertake theoretical and computational studies of the interaction of selected VOCs with models of the air-water interface and the bulk of an aqueous aerosol. The key techniques to be employed will involve the training of machine-learned interatomic potentials for the VOC and its interaction with water in different conditions (air-water interface, bulk, but also in the upper part of the 90-10 region of an interface). Ground-state dynamics – quantum-thermostat Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics and path-integral molecular dynamics – will be used to sample the ground-state nuclear distribution for the selected VOCs for the different environments. Photoabsorption cross-sections will be calculated from these distributions following intense benchmarking of the level of electronic-structure theory.

You should apply if

The position would best suit a talented, motivated, and curious early career researcher with a Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry or Physics and experience in theoretical research of atmospherically related compounds in a complex environment. Some or all of the following skills and experience would be an advantage: experience in using classical molecular dynamics, Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics, path-integral dynamics, and/or development of machine-learned interatomic potentials; experience with coding and scripting for data analysis; ability to communicate complex information clearly and accurately in English, both in written and oral forms; ability to work independently and as part of a team.

postings.advert_text:
The Cambridge Stem Cell Institute is an international centre of excellence for stem cell research and regenerative medicine. Scientists in the Institute collaborate to advance our knowledge of various stem cell types and to perform pioneering work in translational research areas, providing the foundation for new medical treatments (https://www.stemcells.cam.ac.uk/).

The laboratory of Prof. Thóra Káradóttir (https://www.stemcells.cam.ac.uk/people/pi/karadottir) investigates how changes in myelin affect neuronal circuit function, and how myelin loss contributes to neurodegenerative disease. Using a multidisciplinary approach, the group focuses on understanding the cellular and molecular mechanisms that regulate myelination in both health and disease.

A major area of research in the Káradóttir lab focuses on oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs), lineage-committed progenitor cells that proliferate and differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes. The lab has made significant contributions to our understanding of neuron-OPC communication, demonstrating that OPCs can sense neuronal activity directly through neurotransmitter receptors and that this activity-dependent communication regulates OPC state, thereby promoting adaptive myelination and remyelination.

To investigate the mechanisms underlying OPC-neuronal communication and activity-dependent myelination, the group combines in vivo and in vitro approaches with electrophysiology, genetic tools, and advanced imaging techniques. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings are used to characterise the activity, composition, and developmental expression of neurotransmitter receptors in OPCs, while transgenic mouse models enable temporal control of receptor subunit expression.

The successful candidate will investigate the role of NMDA receptor subunits in regulating OPC state and function across the lifespan. Using a combination of whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and Patch-seq, they will characterise age-dependent changes in NMDA receptor-mediated signalling and determine how these changes influence the ability of OPCs to detect and respond to neuronal activity. They will also identify the downstream molecular pathways regulated by NMDA receptor activation and define how these pathways contribute to OPC function at different stages of life.

Requirements

Successful applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in Neuroscience or a closely related discipline. A strong background in transgenic mouse models, whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology of OPCs, and analysis of electrophysiological data is essential. Expertise in myelin biology and experience with Patch-seq methodologies would be an advantage. The successful candidate will be highly organised, capable of working both independently and collaboratively, and able to communicate scientific findings effectively to a range of audiences.

Our Mission

 

Coventry University is a global Education Group that empowers students and communities to transform their lives and society through teaching, learning, research, and enterprise.

The Role

 

As a Research Fellow within the Centre for Agroecology, Water and Resilience (CAWR) you will undertake and play a role in the development of impactful research, contributing to the UKRI-funded project “H2R: Portable Circular System for Greywater & Rainwater Treatment and Reuse”. This post will be based at the Centre for Agroecology, Water and Resilience (CAWR), Coventry University. 

 

In this role you will support research activities in the H2R project on building and bench-testing the integrated H2R prototype and undertaking water quality analysis at CAWR's High-Performance Analytical Hub, and planning and delivering field trials on two sites (in London and Coventry). This will also include sampling, sample preparation, and analysis of influents and effluents from the integrated H2R system for target water quality parameters (pH, turbidity, E. coli, BOD, COD, ionic/elemental/organic pollutant composition, etc.), using standard methods and a range of instrumental techniques, including Ion Chromatography (IC), Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES), Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS), and Liquid Chromatography High-Resolution Mass Spectrometry (LC-HRMS).

 

You will be responsible for developing and contributing to research activities that enhance both individual and collaborative research outputs, contributing to research excellence with national and international impact. •    operating analytical instruments, ideally including IC, ICP-OES, ICP-MS and LC-HRMS, for determining ionic, elemental and organic pollutants, including trace-level and emerging contaminants;
•    IT packages and instrument software for acquiring, processing and interpreting data, and of statistical and data analysis tools (e.g. Excel, R, Python or similar).

 

You will have a track record of high-quality, peer-reviewed publications relative to career stage, and excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present research findings to academic, industrial and community audiences. You will work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team, managing your time to meet project milestones. About the role

Our mission is simple to summarise: make Singapore's healthcare ecosystem measurably harder to attack. We are looking for talented and driven people who will work with us on this mission by finding real weaknesses, building real defenses and see them through to fixes that protect patients, hospitals, and the devices they depend on. 

Imperial College London and Nanyang Technological University (NTU) are seeking a hands-on Cybersecurity Researcher to join IN-CYPHER (Imperial/NTU CYber Protection for HEalthcaRe). IN-CYPHER is a UK–Singapore research programme on the security of connected medical devices and healthcare systems, based at Imperial Global Singapore (IGS). 

What you would be doing

Connected medical devices often stay in service for 10–20 years, are hard to patch, and sit inside complex hospital networks. We want someone who knows how these systems are broken and how they are defended, and who can turn that skill into lasting impact through research, vulnerability disclosure, tooling, and work with clinical and industry partners. 

We welcome candidates whose strengths lie in any of the following areas: 

Red team: penetration testing, vulnerability research, and exploit development, with a record of reported CVEs or published exploits/PoCs. 
Blue team: detection engineering, network monitoring, intrusion and anomaly detection, and incident response, with evidence such as tools, detection pipelines, or deployed infrastructure. 
Yellow team: building the environments others attack and defend, such as cyber ranges, testbeds, vulnerable-by-design systems, and emulation or simulation infrastructure, with evidence of systems you have built. 

Prior medical-domain experience is welcome but not required. You will work closely with clinical and engineering partners at Imperial, NTU, the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine, and Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust. 

Candidates will be employed by Imperial Global Singapore, a research division of Imperial College London, which is consistently ranked within the top 10 of the QS University Rankings.  

The position is based at the Imperial Global Singapore office located in the CREATE building on the NUS campus. The Cybersecurity Researcher will join a vibrant cross-faculty interdisciplinary research environment currently hosting approximately 30 researchers working across 5 major programmes.  

What we are looking for

PhD (or equivalent industrial experience) in computer science, engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.
Practical experience in network security, including protocol analysis, traffic capture, and network-level attack or defence.
Solid understanding of attack techniques and defensive controls across network, system, and application layers, for example MITRE ATT&CK.
Knowledge of research methods and of how to evaluate security techniques rigorously.

The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity.
As a member of staff you will be entitled to leisure facilities within the CREATE building.
Opportunity to travel to Imperial in London or conferences
Generous annual leave entitlement of 21 days plus extra closure days between Christmas and New Year.
Be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture.

About Us

The TOUR (Transforming cancer OUtcomes through Research) team is committed to improving patient outcomes by translating oncology research into clinical practice, with a strong emphasis on patient-centred care and quality of life. Led by Professor Mieke Van Hemelrijck, the team includes a diverse group of researchers—spanning qualitative and quantitative disciplines—alongside clinicians, students, research nurses, and trial coordinators. Together, they work across a wide range of translational oncology projects, with a particular focus on the development and implementation of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). 

A key strand of TOUR’s work involves collaboration with the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life Group, where the team contributes to the development and validation of tools to assess health-related quality of life in cancer patients. These projects often involve international partnerships and span a variety of cancer types and treatment contexts.

This post will support the studies with the EORTC as well as a collaborative quality of life research project with The Royal Marsden Hospital (RMH), focusing on the integration of patient perspectives into cancer care. The successful candidate will be based within the TOUR team and will hold an honorary contract with The Royal Marsden**,** enabling access to data and facilitating close collaboration with clinical and research colleagues across both institutions – including the Sutton hospital site of RMH.

Please note that this role will involve regular travel to the Royal Marsden Hospital in Sutton. 

About The Role

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Research Assistant to join the TOUR (Transforming cancer OUtcomes through Research) team at Guy’s Cancer. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to internationally recognised research focused on improving the quality of life for people living with and beyond cancer.

The role will involve close collaboration with clinical teams and international partners, including the EORTC Quality of Life Group**,** to ensure that patient perspectives are meaningfully integrated into cancer care and research. The successful candidate will also support a collaborative project with The Royal Marsden Hospital, with a specific focus on the development and implementation of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and identified supportive care needs.

Reporting to Professor Mieke Van Hemelrijck and the senior TOUR team, the post holder will be responsible for providing administrative and project management support across the quality of life research portfolio. Key responsibilities include coordinating ethics submissions, supporting patient recruitment and qualitative interviews, managing study documentation, and assisting with data collection and analysis. The role will also involve liaising with internal and external stakeholders to ensure smooth project delivery.

This position offers an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in health, psychology, or a related discipline who is passionate about patient-centred research. An understanding of qualitative research methods and data protection regulations (e.g. GDPR) is essential, as is the ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will be based at Guy’s Cancer Centre and will also hold an honorary contract with The Royal Marsden Hospital, enabling access to data and facilitating collaboration across both institutions – including on site visits to the Sutton hospital site of RMH.

If you are enthusiastic about improving cancer care through high-quality research and want to be part of a dynamic and supportive team, we encourage you to apply.

This is a full time / part time post (35 Hours per week), and you will be offered an indefinite / a fixed term contract until 31/12/2027.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential Criteria 

Candidates must demonstrate the following:

BSc in a health, psychology, or data-related discipline (or pending completion).
Experience supporting research studies with rigorous attention to detail, including ethics submissions and participant recruitment.
Understanding of both qualitative and quantitative research methods in the context of applied health research.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to summarise and present research findings.
Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines, and operate within regulatory frameworks.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and familiarity with qualitative or mixed-methods data tools (e.g. NVivo, Excel, REDCap, SPSS).
Knowledge of GDPR, the Data Protection Act, and best practices in data confidentiality and security.
Ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partners.
Desirable Criteria 

The following are not essential but will strengthen an application:

Experience conducting or supporting qualitative interviews.
Familiarity with patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) or quality of life questionnaires.
Experience working in a clinical or academic research environment – with a specific focus on the National Health Services (NHS).
Ability to work independently and adapt to changing priorities.
Interest in oncology, survivorship, or patient-centred research.

We are seeking an ambitious and creative experimental physical scientist to join our group as a founding member of the UKRI-funded Future Leaders Fellowship project ‘Transition State Imaging’. The project will build an Anion Reaction Microscope, a novel anion spectrometer for time-resolved Coulomb explosion imaging experiments in our group’s laboratory.
This instrument will generate a beam of mass-selected molecular and/or cluster anions and will image the ultrafast nuclear dynamics triggered by photodetachment of the excess electron, using a new high-repetition rate Ytterbium laser system. These unique capabilities will advance our fundamental understanding of chemical reactivity by extending the time-resolved Coulomb explosion imaging technique beyond unimolecular photochemistry and towards new chemical contexts, e.g. bi-molecular reactions, solvent dynamics, and electron-induced chemistry.

Specifically, the candidate will be involved in:
 Design and commissioning of the anion reaction microscope
 Development of femtosecond laser beamlines
 Scientific investigations into nuclear dynamics of photodetachment from prototypical anions

 The candidate must have (or be about to) complete a PhD in in physical chemistry, chemical physics, atomic, molecular and optical physics, or a closely related discipline.– with demonstratable expertise in one or more of the following areas: mass spectrometry techniques, ultrafast spectroscopy, charged particle detection/imaging, and/or scientific instrument development.

 What we offer:
 We are a new research group, and this position offers an unprecedented opportunity for the right person to make a major intellectual contribution to a unique research programme at the forefront of chemical dynamics. As such, this is an ideal role for an early career researcher who is looking to apply their technical expertise and demonstrate their scientific creativity, in a supportive and collaborative team environment.

 We are committed to your own professional and scientific development. The project is supported by partnerships with leading experimental and theoretical research groups and facilities in Europe (EuXFEL-SQS) and the UK (Universities of Birmingham-List Group and East Anglia-Bull Group); there will be ample opportunities for external support, collaboration, and space to allow the candidate to develop their own research activities within the parameters of the project.

 The role is offered on a full-time (36.25 hours per week), fixed-term basis for an initial period of 12-months, but extendable up to 48-months, upon mutual agreement. The salary band, for candidates who hold a PhD at the time of commencement, begins at £35,608 p.a. Candidates who have not had their doctorates conferred will begin at £32,080 p.a., moving onto the higher band upon degree conferral.

 All informal inquires are welcome, and should be addressed to Dr Patrick Robertson, (patrick.robertson@nottingham.ac.uk). More information about our research group can be found on the group website, www.nurd.org.uk.

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an enthusiastic, student-centred French specialist to join Modern Languages, Translation and Interpreting (MLTI) as a Teaching Fellow on a fixed-term, five-month contract at 0.8 FTE. This semester-long post is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to build their university teaching experience in a supportive and collegial department.

You will teach French language across a range of proficiency levels, together with translation and/or interpreting, to undergraduate and postgraduate students. You will set and mark assessments, give timely and constructive feedback, act as a Personal Tutor and contribute to open days and outreach. The role is focused entirely on teaching and the student experience, so there is no expectation of research beyond what supports your teaching.

MLTI is part of the School of Culture and Communication and is based at Singleton Campus, beside Singleton Park and a short walk from Swansea Bay. We bring language, culture, translation and interpreting together under one roof, teaching across our undergraduate degrees and our postgraduate programmes in translation and interpreting. We are a friendly, multilingual and international team who care about our students and about one another, and our small-group language teaching means you will get to know your students well.

If you are passionate about French and about helping students grow in confidence as linguists, translators and interpreters, we would love to hear from you.

EQUALITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

The University is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity in all its practices and activities. We aim to establish an inclusive environment and welcome diverse applications from the following protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic and national origin), religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.

As an inclusive and welcoming workplace, we value people for their skills regardless of their background. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English.

WELSH LANGUAGE SKILLS

The Welsh language level required for this role is Level 1 - A little. The role holder will be able to pronounce Welsh words, answer the phone in Welsh (good morning/afternoon) and use very basic everyday words and phrases (thank you, please etc.). Level 1 can be reached by completing a 1 hour course.

The University is a proud bilingual institution, our Welsh Language Strategy outlines our aspiration to promote the language and enable our staff to engage with the language as an additional workplace skill and as a gateway to new cultural and social opportunities. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English. Welsh speakers have the right to an interview in Welsh. Applicants for a role where Welsh skills are essential are expected to present their application in Welsh and will be interviewed in Welsh, if shortlisted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Applications for this role will take the format of a CV submission and cover letter.

In your cover letter, please explain how you meet the essential and desirable criteria in the job description, giving concrete examples from your teaching experience.

This is a fixed-term post covering one semester, with an anticipated start date of 25/01/2027.
